title: Customization and Taxonomies
summary: Documents IP source management, vulnerability category setup, and checklist/template customization.
coverage: Managing IP source groups and scope
Keeping taxonomy aligned with reporting outputs

warning.title: IMPORTANT
paragraphs: Taxonomy and template changes modify future operator behavior and report output quality. Validate changes in a controlled test record before broad rollout.

sections.title: IP source governance model
paragraphs: IP source mapping links concrete IP addresses to operational source groups. This labeling is part of inventory governance and directly impacts filtering and triage in records workflows.
The settings UI stages additions and deletions in memory and applies them only on `Submit Changes`, allowing admins to review a batch before commit.

rows: Matching `records.ip_address` rows get `source=<group>`, `status=updated`, and refreshed modification timestamp.
Matching rows are reverted to `source=Other`, `status=updated`, and refreshed modification timestamp.

sections.title: IP source change flow
paragraphs: Use source groups for durable provenance labels such as scanner domain, ingestion channel, or network segment. Avoid temporary labels that cannot survive long-term analytics.
For each source group, add or remove IPs, then submit in one batch. This keeps source transition events coherent and easier to audit.

Add or remove IP addresses in the right-side panel.
Review staged changes and click `Submit Changes`.
Refresh records list and verify `source` and `status` updates on impacted records.

sections.title: Vulnerability category taxonomy
paragraphs: Vulnerability categories are stored in `vuln_categories` and exposed in pentest workflows for standardized classification. A stable category model improves trend and reporting consistency.
Category creation and deletion are permission-gated by `manage_vuln_categories`. Duplicate names are rejected by backend uniqueness constraints.

Supports audit traceability for taxonomy lifecycle.

sections.title: Checklist template governance
paragraphs: Checklist templates define service-specific test coverage and optional auto-enable ports. They are managed under `Checklist Templates` and written to `service_checklists`.
System templates cannot be deleted. Admins can customize them and later reset to canonical definitions when drift must be removed.

sections.title: Report template administration
paragraphs: Report templates are managed in Settings and stored in `report_templates`. Enabled templates appear in pentest report generation selectors, while disabled templates remain available for management when permission allows.
Template definition validation enforces non-empty block arrays and normalized block types. System templates support canonical reset and protect immutable key semantics.

sections.title: Recommended taxonomy operating cadence
paragraphs: Treat taxonomy and template governance as a recurring operations task instead of ad-hoc edits. A predictable cadence reduces schema drift and reporting inconsistency.
orderedList: Review new source groups and category additions weekly.
Validate checklist auto-port mappings against real service exposure monthly.
Review report template enabled set and canonical drift before each reporting cycle.
Document every taxonomy or template change in the operational change log.
